newsitem.title: FRENCH GUIANA: Guiana independence leader charged with arson.
newsitem.headline: Guiana independence leader charged with arson.

text.p: A leading member of French Guiana's independence movement has been charged with arson following his detention by French police, local state-owned radio said on Monday.

The radio said that Alain Michel and four others were charged with setting fire to the home of French Guiana's state prosecutor Jean-Luc Beck during riots in November. They have also been charged with violence against a magistrate exercising his duty.
Judicial sources said they face up to 20 years in jail if convicted.

Michel, a founder and spokesman of the Guiana National Popular Party (PNPG), was held on Friday in French Guiana's capital Cayenne and was taken with the four others on Saturday to the French Caribbean island of Martinique aboard a military aircraft.
The alleged arsonists were flown to Martinique to enable a public prosecutor, not personally involved in the incident, to proceed with prosecution.

Beck's home was attacked during riots that shook the French overseas department during four days last November. French officials described the riots as "a deliberate attempt to destabilise French Guiana."

French Guiana, on the northeast coast of South America, is the only non-independent territory on the mainland of the Western Hemisphere. Its economy is heavily dependent on subsidies from France and 23 percent of the population of 150,000 is unemployed.
The PNPG favours independence from France.
The European Space Agency (ESA) Ariane rocket launch site is located in Kourou, French Guiana, 72 km (50 miles) from Cayenne.
